findings.claim: The supplied learning/score support is the closed window [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score times at 0.01 spacing from 0.0 to 0.49; the curve-support audit reports a selected-count fraction of 0.49 of that window, so coordinate evidence covers only the first 49% of the declared learning window and the remainder is unobserved rather than absent.

Label semantics are 'Recorded affinities removed; equal score prior', so the observed score times carry no decoded affinity labels; selection preference in this window cannot be read as descendant survival or measured final affinity benefit.

The coordinate representation is native model endpoint world coordinates, and the incumbent reward view is an endpoint pointcloud with a FLOWR endpoint VJP derivative path; the coordinate proxy is untyped, so no energy or chemical-interaction meaning is attached to it here.

hypotheses.direction: W1_early_soft: reduced early-window coordinate change, increased late-window coordinate change relative to W3_early_strong_control; both arms share the same M2 reward and equal integral of RMS ratios.
hypotheses.falsifier: No significant difference in the landmark coordinate features between W1_early_soft and W3_early_strong_control at matched score times, or a difference in the opposite direction to the stated early/late contrast.
hypotheses.observable: Per-landmark local coordinate features (landmark_XX_local_dx/dy/dz and local_cxx..czz) and soft_mass sampled at the registered score times, compared between the two dose arms.
hypotheses.scope: Global endpoint coordinate field across all 20 landmarks over the observed window [0.0, 0.49].
hypotheses.statement: A temporal dose recipe that redistributes the ratio budget toward later score nodes (W1_early_soft) versus the opposite time-order control (W3_early_strong_control) will produce a measurable difference in the endpoint coordinate trajectory over the observed window, with the early-soft arm showing lower early-window coordinate displacement and higher late-window displacement than the early-strong arm.

hypotheses.direction: Peak in |d(coordinate)/dt| near the middle of the observed window for W2_middle_peak relative to the monotone-decreasing (W3) and monotone-increasing (W1) dose profiles.
hypotheses.falsifier: Coordinate change rate for W2_middle_peak is flat or extremal at the window endpoints rather than mid-window.
hypotheses.observable: Time derivative of landmark local coordinate features across the registered score times, compared against the W1 and W3 arms.
hypotheses.scope: Global endpoint coordinate field across all 20 landmarks over the observed window [0.0, 0.49].
hypotheses.statement: A middle-emphasis dose recipe (W2_middle_peak) will show a non-monotone coordinate displacement profile over the observed window, with the largest per-step coordinate change concentrated near the middle score nodes rather than at the window endpoints.

limitations: Temporal profiles are not available in this packet (temporal_profiles_available=false), so no per-time coordinate profile could be read; the hypotheses above are stated as testable contrasts, not as observed effects.
The curve-support audit reports only 0.49 of the declared [0.0, 0.5] learning window as selected; the remaining 0.01 of the window is unobserved and no extrapolation is licensed.
Decoded affinity labels are absent (recorded affinities removed), so no finding here links coordinate change to final predicted target affinity, validity, or strain.
The registered dose recipes are predeclared interventions, not discovered biological stages; the knot placement is an experimental hypothesis and no stage boundary is inferred from it.
No current study quality outcomes are available to the Analyst, so no claim is made about which dose arm performs better on the primary objective.
